Course Code: CSL100
Title: Introduction to Programming
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.5 (L-T-P: 2-1-3)
Semester Offered: Semester 1
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial + Practical
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Introduction to Programming is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL100 - Introduction to Programming
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.5
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Basics of programming using C; Basic UNIX commands, Primitives and Datatypes, Arithmetic operations, Input and output functions; Conditional statement; Loops, Introduction to Functions, Macros, Recursion, Arrays, Strings, Dynamic Memory Allocation, Pointers, Complex Data Types, File Handling, Introduction to Linked List, sorting, Searching, Bitwise Operator.

Course Code: MAL100
Title: Mathematics-I
Department: Mathematics
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 1
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Mathematics-I is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Mathematics at IIT Bhilai.

Course: MAL100 - Mathematics-I
Department: Mathematics | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Differential and Integral Calculus: Rolle's theorem, Mean value theorems, Taylor's and Maclaurin theorems, Maxima and minima, Indeterminate forms; Linear Algebra: Matrices, Systems of linear equations, Gauss elimination, Vector spaces, Subspaces, Linear independence, Basis and dimension, Linear transformations, Eigenvalues, eigenvectors, Diagonalization, Cayley-Hamilton Theorem.

Course Code: PHL101
Title: Physics for Engineers
Department: Physics
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 1
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Physics for Engineers is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Physics at IIT Bhilai.

Course: PHL101 - Physics for Engineers
Department: Physics | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Classical Mechanics, Oscillations and Waves: Simple harmonic motion, Damped and driven oscillators, Resonance; Quantum Mechanics: Wave-particle duality, De Broglie hypothesis, Heisenberg uncertainty principle, Schrodinger wave equation, Particle in a box; Optics and Lasers: Interference, Diffraction, Polarization, Principles of Lasers and optical fibers.

Course Code: CYL100
Title: Applied Chemistry
Department: Chemistry
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 1
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Applied Chemistry is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Chemistry at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CYL100 - Applied Chemistry
Department: Chemistry | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Molecular structure and spectroscopy; Thermodynamics and chemical kinetics; Electrochemistry and corrosion; Polymer chemistry and smart materials; Nanomaterials and green chemistry principles for modern engineering applications.

Course Code: MEP102
Title: Digital Fabrication
Department: Mechanical Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 1-0.5-3)
Semester Offered: Semester 2
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Digital Fabrication is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Mechanical Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: MEP102 - Digital Fabrication
Department: Mechanical Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction to Computer-Aided Design (CAD), 3D printing technologies (FDM, SLA), CNC machining, laser cutting, PCB prototyping, rapid tooling, and integration of mechanical fabrication with digital electronics.

Course Code: EEL101
Title: Basic Electrical Engineering
Department: Electrical Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 2
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Basic Electrical Engineering is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Electrical Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: EEL101 - Basic Electrical Engineering
Department: Electrical Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
DC Circuit analysis, Thevenin and Norton theorems, Maximum power transfer theorem; AC circuits, Phasors, Single-phase and three-phase circuits, Power and power factor; Magnetic circuits and Transformers; DC machines and Induction motors.

Course Code: ECL101
Title: Basic Electronics Engineering
Department: Electronics & Communication Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 2
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Basic Electronics Engineering is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Electronics & Communication Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: ECL101 - Basic Electronics Engineering
Department: Electronics & Communication Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Semiconductor physics, p-n junction diodes, Zener diodes, diode circuits and rectifiers; Bipolar Junction Transistors (BJTs) and Field Effect Transistors (FETs, MOSFETs); Operational Amplifiers (Op-Amps) and linear/non-linear applications; Digital logic basics, logic gates, truth tables, and boolean minimization.

Course Code: MAL101
Title: Mathematics-II
Department: Mathematics
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 2
Curriculum Category: Institute Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Mathematics-II is an official Institute Core course offered by the Department of Mathematics at IIT Bhilai.

Course: MAL101 - Mathematics-II
Department: Mathematics | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Multivariable Calculus: Functions of several variables, partial derivatives, directional derivatives, gradient, curl, divergence, line, surface, and volume integrals, Green's, Stokes', and Gauss divergence theorems; Ordinary Differential Equations: First-order ODEs, higher-order linear ODEs with constant coefficients, series solutions, Laplace transforms.

Course Code: MAL403
Title: Probability & Statistics
Department: Mathematics
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 3
Curriculum Category: Program Linked
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Probability & Statistics is an official Program Linked course offered by the Department of Mathematics at IIT Bhilai.

Course: MAL403 - Probability & Statistics
Department: Mathematics | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Probability theory: Axioms of probability, Conditional probability, Bayes' theorem; Random variables and distributions (discrete and continuous): Binomial, Poisson, Geometric, Uniform, Exponential, Normal; Joint distributions, covariance, correlation; Sampling distributions, Central Limit Theorem; Estimation, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, regression analysis.

Course Code: CSL201
Title: Discrete Mathematics
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 3
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: None
Summary: Discrete Mathematics is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL201 - Discrete Mathematics
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Sets, relations, functions, Equivalence and Partial order relations; Formal logic: Propositional logic and truth tables, normal forms, Predicates and Quantification; Notion of proof: proof techniques, Mathematical Induction; Combinatorics: Basic counting techniques, The pigeonhole principle, countable and uncountable sets, recurrence relations, The principle of Inclusion-exclusion; Graph theory: Graph terminology, representation of graphs, Isomorphism, trees, Eulerian and Hamiltonian graphs, Graph coloring and Planar graphs; Number theory: Divisibility, GCD, The Euclidean algorithm, The fundamental theorem of arithmetic, Modular arithmetic; Group theory: Groups, subgroups, finite groups, cyclic groups, permutation groups.

Course Code: CSL202
Title: Data Structures
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 2-1-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 3
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL100 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Data Structures is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL202 - Data Structures
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Stacks, Queues, Lists; Sorting and Searching; Trees, Tree Traversals; Heaps, Priority Queues; Binary Search, Binary Search Trees, Balanced BSTs (AVL, Red-Black Trees); Hashing and Hash Tables; Graphs: Representations, Depth First Search, Breadth First Search, Topological Sort.

Course Code: CSP203
Title: Software Tools & Technologies Lab
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 1-0-4)
Semester Offered: Semester 3
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL100 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Software Tools & Technologies Lab is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSP203 - Software Tools & Technologies Lab
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Basics of Linux: Linux commands, shell scripting, text editors (Vim/Emacs); Scripting languages (Python/Bash); Web programming (HTML, CSS, JS, REST APIs); Plotting tools (Gnuplot, Matplotlib); Document processing tools (LaTeX, Markdown); Version control systems (Git, GitHub workflows); Debuggers (gdb, valgrind); Containerization with Docker.

Course Code: CSL251
Title: Computer Organization and Architecture
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 4
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL100 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), ECL101 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Computer Organization and Architecture is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL251 - Computer Organization and Architecture
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction: Overview of basic digital building blocks, truth tables, basic structure of a digital computer, number representation; Machine Instructions and Program: Assembly language programming for processors; Arithmetic Unit: Basic building blocks for the ALU, adder, subtractor, shifter, multiplication and division circuits, control path microprogramming, hardwired control; Memory organization: ROM, RAM, EPROM, Flash, cache memories, cache coherence protocol for uniprocessor, virtual memory, secondary storage; Input/Output Organization: I/O subblock, interrupts, polling, DMA; Pipelining: Instruction pipeline, hazards and forwarding.

Course Code: CSL252
Title: Design and Analysis of Algorithms
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 4
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: CSL100 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSL201 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSL202 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Design and Analysis of Algorithms is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL252 - Design and Analysis of Algorithms
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Algorithm analysis: worst and average case, asymptotic notation, recurrences; Sorting and selection: randomized quicksort, median finding; Randomized techniques; Divide and Conquer; Dynamic programming and Greedy algorithms; Graph algorithms: BFS, DFS, Minimum Spanning Trees (Prim, Kruskal), Shortest paths (Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall), Network Flow (Ford-Fulkerson); NP-Completeness, reductions, and introduction to Approximation Algorithms.

Course Code: CSL253
Title: Theory of Computation
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-1-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 4
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Tutorial
Prerequisites: CSL201 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSL202 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Theory of Computation is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL253 - Theory of Computation
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Alphabets, languages, finite automata (DFA, NFA, regular expressions, pumping lemma for regular languages); Context-Free Grammars and Context-Free Languages, parse trees, pushdown automata, CYK algorithm, pumping lemma for CFLs; Turing machines, Church-Turing thesis, decidability, halting problem, reductions; Introduction to space and time complexity, P vs NP, NP-completeness.

Course Code: CSL301
Title: Operating Systems
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 5
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL202 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSL251 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Operating Systems is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL301 - Operating Systems
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction: Virtualization, Concurrency, Persistence; CPU Virtualization: Process, Process API, PCB, mechanism, CPU scheduling, Multilevel Feedback Queue; Memory Virtualization: Address space, memory API, address translation, segmentation, paging, TLBs, replacement policies, swapping; Concurrency: Threads, thread API, locks, condition variables, semaphores, concurrency bugs; Persistence: I/O devices, Hard disks, RAID, file and directories, file system implementation; Security: OS security, authentication, access control; Practical tools and kernel hacking with xv6.

Course Code: CSL302
Title: Compiler Design
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 5
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL251 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSL253 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Compiler Design is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL302 - Compiler Design
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Compiler structure: Analysis-synthesis model of compilation, phases of a compiler, tool-based approach to compiler construction; Phases of compiler design: Lexical analysis (Lex/Flex); Syntax analysis (LL, LR, LALR parsing, Yacc/Bison); Syntax-directed translation; Type checking and semantic analysis; Run-time system and memory layout; Intermediate code generation (Three-address code, SSA); Machine-independent optimizations (dead code elimination, loop optimizations); Target code generation and register allocation.

Course Code: CSL303
Title: Database Management Systems
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 5
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL202 (PrerequisiteKind.RECOMMENDED)
Summary: Database Management Systems is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL303 - Database Management Systems
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Database System Concepts: Data models, schemas and instances, database languages, relational DBMS architecture; Relational Algebra: Select, Project, Set operations, Join, Division; ER and EER Models: Entities, relationships, keys, specialization/generalization, schema mapping; Normalization: Functional dependencies, 1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF, multivalued dependencies and 4NF; Transaction Management: ACID properties, serializability, concurrency control (2PL, timestamp ordering), recovery systems (WAL, checkpoints); Indexing: B+ Trees, hashing; SQL programming and database application development.

Course Code: CSL304
Title: Artificial Intelligence
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 5
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL202 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), MAL403 (PrerequisiteKind.RECOMMENDED)
Summary: Artificial Intelligence is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL304 - Artificial Intelligence
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction and Agent Architectures; Problem Solving by Search: Uninformed search (BFS, DFS), Informed search (A*, IDA*), Heuristics, Adversarial search (Minimax, Alpha-Beta pruning), Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP); Automated Reasoning: Propositional and First-Order Logic, inference, resolution refutation, knowledge-based systems; Planning: Classical planning, STRIPS, state-space and plan-space planning; Reasoning under Uncertainty: Probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian networks, inference; Reinforcement Learning: Markov Decision Processes (MDP), Bellman equations, Value/Policy iteration, Q-learning.

Course Code: CSL351
Title: Computer Networks
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 4.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-2)
Semester Offered: Semester 6
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL301 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Computer Networks is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL351 - Computer Networks
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 4.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction: Layered architecture (OSI, TCP/IP), packet switching vs circuit switching, delay, loss, and throughput; Application Layer: HTTP, DNS, SMTP, P2P, CDNs; Transport Layer: TCP, UDP, reliable data transfer, flow control, congestion control (TCP Reno, Cubic, BBR), socket programming; Network Layer: IP addressing, subnetting, CIDR, NAT, routing algorithms (Dijkstra, Distance Vector), BGP, OSPF, ICMP, IPv6; Data Link Layer: Framing, error detection/correction, MAC protocols (CSMA/CD, CSMA/CA), Ethernet, Wi-Fi; Network Security: TLS/SSL, IPSec, firewalls; Simulation tools: Wireshark, NS-3, Mininet.

Course Code: CSP352
Title: AI-Augmented Software Development
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 1-0-4)
Semester Offered: Semester 6
Curriculum Category: Program Core
Instruction Mode: Lecture + Practical
Prerequisites: CSL100 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSP203 (PrerequisiteKind.RECOMMENDED)
Summary: AI-Augmented Software Development is an official Program Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSP352 - AI-Augmented Software Development
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction to LLM-based software engineering: Role of LLMs in SDLC, coding assistants, testing and debugging support, documentation, academic integrity; Prompting as interface design: Role and task specification, constraints, structured prompting, prompt refinement; LLMs as software components: LLM APIs, request/response patterns, context handling, schema validation; From assistants to agents: Perceive-think-act-observe loops, tool use, single-agent task execution, tool registries; Agent harness engineering: Harness definition, bounded execution, step limits, runtime policies, trace logging, human-in-the-loop approvals; Evaluation harnesses: Task suites, success criteria, regression testing, step count and latency metrics; Safety and governance: Prompt injection, unsafe tool use, sandboxing, human review; Capstone team project.

Course Code: CSP402
Title: Nand to Tetris
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 2.0 (L-T-P: 0-0-4)
Semester Offered: Semester 6
Curriculum Category: Program Elective
Instruction Mode: Practical
Prerequisites: CSL251 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Nand to Tetris is an official Program Elective course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSP402 - Nand to Tetris
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 2.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Building a modern computer from first principles: Boolean logic, logic gates, ALU design; Sequential logic, flip-flops, memory units; Machine language, Hack computer architecture; Assembly language and Hack assembler implementation; Virtual machine abstraction, stack arithmetic, memory segments, VM translator; High-level object-based language (Jack); Jack compiler (syntax analysis, code generation); Mini-operating system implementation.

Course Code: CSL505
Title: Cryptography
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 7
Curriculum Category: Program Elective
Instruction Mode: Lecture
Prerequisites: CSL201 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD), CSL351 (PrerequisiteKind.RECOMMENDED)
Summary: Cryptography is an official Program Elective course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL505 - Cryptography
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction, Formal Notions, Mathematics Recap, Historical Ciphers; Attack Models, Informational and Computational Security, Perfect Secrecy; Symmetric Key Cryptography: Stream ciphers (LFSR), Block ciphers (DES, AES), Modes of operation; Cryptanalysis: Linear and Differential Cryptanalysis; Hash Functions: SHA-2, SHA-3, HMAC, collisions, Birthday paradox; Public Key Cryptography: RSA, Diffie-Hellman, Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC); Digital Signatures and PKI; Quantum Cryptography overview.

Course Code: CSL510
Title: Approximation Algorithms
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 7
Curriculum Category: Program Elective
Instruction Mode: Lecture
Prerequisites: CSL252 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: Approximation Algorithms is an official Program Elective course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL510 - Approximation Algorithms
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Introduction to NP-completeness and approximation algorithms; Combinatorial algorithms: Greedy algorithms (Set Cover), Local search (Facility Location); Rounding data and Dynamic Programming (Knapsack FPTAS); Linear Programming (LP) relaxations and LP duality; Deterministic rounding and randomized rounding; Primal-dual schema (Vertex Cover, Network Design); Metric embeddings; Semidefinite Programming (Max-Cut); Hardness of approximation and PCP theorem overview.

Course Code: CSQ401
Title: BTech Project-I
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 0-0-6)
Semester Offered: Semester 7
Curriculum Category: Capstone Core
Instruction Mode: Project
Prerequisites: None
Summary: BTech Project-I is an official Capstone Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSQ401 - BTech Project-I
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Research and development-oriented capstone project based on problems of practical and theoretical interest under faculty supervision. Includes comprehensive literature survey, formulation of research methodology/system architecture, baseline experiments, interim evaluation, and written report.

Course Code: CSQ402
Title: BTech Project-II
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 0-0-6)
Semester Offered: Semester 8
Curriculum Category: Capstone Core
Instruction Mode: Project
Prerequisites: CSQ401 (PrerequisiteKind.HARD)
Summary: BTech Project-II is an official Capstone Core course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSQ402 - BTech Project-II
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Continuation of CSQ401: full implementation, experimental validation, comparative benchmark analysis, final software prototype or scientific paper manuscript, public defense presentation, and comprehensive thesis submission.

Course Code: CSL495
Title: MOOC-based (NPTEL): Advanced Computer Science
Department: Computer Science and Engineering
Credits: 3.0 (L-T-P: 3-0-0)
Semester Offered: Semester 7
Curriculum Category: Program Elective
Instruction Mode: Online MOOC + Proctored Exam
Prerequisites: None
Summary: MOOC-based (NPTEL): Advanced Computer Science is an official Program Elective course offered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at IIT Bhilai.

Course: CSL495 - MOOC-based (NPTEL): Advanced Computer Science
Department: Computer Science and Engineering | Credits: 3.0
Detailed Syllabus & Learning Objectives:
Departmentally approved NPTEL / SWAYAM advanced 12-week course for credit transfer. Governed under IIT Bhilai MOOC Policy Section 3.2.1. Supervised and evaluated by DUGC Convener.

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_CREDIT_NORMAL_LOAD]
Category: Credit Limits
Applies To: All B.Tech students (Semesters 1 through 8)
Numeric Limit: 18.0
Ordinance Provision:
"The normal semester load for undergraduate B.Tech students is governed by the semester-wise curriculum matrix, typically ranging between 17 and 19.5 credits per regular semester."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_CREDIT_OVERLOAD_MAX]
Category: Credit Limits
Applies To: B.Tech CSE students (Semester 3 to 8)
Numeric Limit: 21.0
Ordinance Provision:
"In general a student has to register for the nominal load as per the semester-wise program curriculum. Overload/underload can only be permitted from third semester onwards. BTech students may be allowed to register up to a maximum of 21 credits from their third semester onwards by the concerned DUGC conveners on a case-to-case basis."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_CREDIT_UNDERLOAD_MIN]
Category: Credit Limits
Applies To: B.Tech CSE students (Semester 3 to 7)
Numeric Limit: 15.0
Ordinance Provision:
"Underload can only be permitted from third semester onwards. BTech students may be allowed to register for a minimum of 15 credits from their third semester onwards by the concerned DUGC conveners on a case-to-case basis."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_CREDIT_FINAL_SEM_MIN]
Category: Credit Limits
Applies To: Graduating B.Tech students (Semester 8)
Numeric Limit: 9.0
Ordinance Provision:
"In the eighth regular semester, BTech students may be allowed to register up to a minimum of 9 credits by the concerned DUGC conveners subject to fulfilling all pending credit requirements."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_GRADUATION_MIN_CREDITS]
Category: Graduation Requirements
Applies To: All B.Tech CSE candidates
Numeric Limit: 144.0
Ordinance Provision:
"To be eligible for the award of a BTech in Computer Science and Engineering degree, a candidate must earn at least 144 course credits (comprising 40.5 Institute Core, 4 Program Linked, 52 Program Core, 22.5 Program Elective, 15 Open Elective, and 10 Liberal Arts) plus 12 Non-Graded Core units, maintaining a minimum CGPA of 4.5."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_PREREQUISITE_CLEARANCE]
Category: Prerequisites
Applies To: All courses with prerequisite constraints
Numeric Limit: N/A
Ordinance Provision:
"Pre-requisites shall be defined only in terms of other course code(s). A precedent course defined as a prerequisite for a course must be cleared (obtaining a passing grade; non-F grade) before the dependent course can be registered."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_NPTEL_MAX_CREDITS]
Category: MOOC / NPTEL Transfer
Applies To: All undergraduate B.Tech students
Numeric Limit: 6.0
Ordinance Provision:
"A student shall be allowed to opt for a maximum of 6 credits from MOOC-based portals (such as NPTEL / SWAYAM) for considering against credit transfer during their entire B.Tech undergraduate program."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_NPTEL_EQUIVALENCE_DURATION]
Category: MOOC / NPTEL Transfer
Applies To: Approved 14-week NPTEL/SWAYAM courses
Numeric Limit: 3.0
Ordinance Provision:
"A 14-week or 42-hour MOOC/NPTEL course shall be considered equivalent to a full-semester course worth 3 credits of IIT Bhilai. Prior departmental DUGC approval is mandatory before enrolling."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_NPTEL_GRADING_PROCEDURE]
Category: MOOC / NPTEL Transfer
Applies To: Students crediting NPTEL courses
Numeric Limit: N/A
Ordinance Provision:
"The respective DUGC convener acts as instructor-in-charge for any approved MOOC-based course (using course code format CSL495). The proctored grade is displayed on the semester grade sheet and counted directly towards CGPA calculation."

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_HONOURS_MINOR_ELIGIBILITY]
Category: Minor Degree & Honours
Applies To: Undergraduate B.Tech students at completion of Semester 5
Numeric Limit: 8.0
Ordinance Provision:
"A student at the end of the 5th semester can apply to register for BTech Honours or Minor specialization in another discipline. Eligibility requires a cumulative CGPA of 8.0 or above, no active backlogs, and successful completion of 24 additional credits beyond the normal 144 credits."

filter_metadata.applies_to: Undergraduate B.Tech students at completion of Semester 5

IIT Bhilai Academic Regulation [RULE_ACADEMIC_PROBATION_SGPA]
Category: Academic Standing
Applies To: All registered undergraduate students

Practice Exercise [EX_DSA_01]
Target Skill: SKILL_TREES_AND_HEAPS
Difficulty Tier: MEDIUM
Problem Statement:
Given an unbalanced Binary Search Tree with n nodes, explain how AVL tree rotations maintain the O(log n) height invariant upon inserting a key that causes an imbalance factor of +2 at node P with a left child having balance factor -1.
Reference Solution & Rubric:
This corresponds to a Left-Right (LR) imbalance case. The restoration requires a double rotation: first a Left Rotation on the left child of P, converting the tree into a Left-Left (LL) case, followed immediately by a Right Rotation on node P. Both rotations update balance factors and restore strict AVL height balance in O(1) rotation time.

Practice Exercise [EX_ALGO_02]
Target Skill: SKILL_DYNAMIC_PROGRAMMING
Difficulty Tier: MEDIUM
Problem Statement:
Formulate the Bellman recurrence relation for the 0/1 Knapsack Problem with capacity W and items (w_i, v_i). State the space complexity optimization technique.
Reference Solution & Rubric:
Recurrence: DP[i, w] = DP[i-1, w] if w_i > w; else max(DP[i-1, w], DP[i-1, w - w_i] + v_i), with base case DP[0, w] = 0. Space can be optimized from O(n*W) to O(W) using a single 1D array traversed backwards from W down to w_i to avoid overwriting values needed from the previous iteration.

Practice Exercise [EX_OS_03]
Target Skill: SKILL_OS_CONCURRENCY
Difficulty Tier: HARD
Problem Statement:
Explain the four Coffman conditions necessary for a deadlock to occur. How does the Banker's algorithm prevent deadlock by denying requests that lead to unsafe states?
Reference Solution & Rubric:
The four Coffman conditions are: 1. Mutual Exclusion, 2. Hold and Wait, 3. No Preemption, 4. Circular Wait. The Banker's algorithm runs a safety check before granting any resource allocation: it simulates allocating the requested resources and verifies whether there exists at least one sequence of process completions where all remaining claims (Need matrix <= Work vector) can be satisfied without deadlock.

Practice Exercise [EX_TOC_04]
Target Skill: SKILL_AUTOMATA_THEORY
Difficulty Tier: EASY
Problem Statement:
Use the Pumping Lemma for Regular Languages to demonstrate that L = {0^n 1^n | n >= 0} is not regular.
Reference Solution & Rubric:
Assume L is regular with pumping length p. Choose string s = 0^p 1^p in L (|s| = 2p >= p). According to the lemma, s = xyz with |xy| <= p and |y| >= 1. Since |xy| <= p, y consists entirely of 0s (y = 0^k, k >= 1). Pumping with i = 2 gives xy^2z = 0^(p+k) 1^p. Since k >= 1, the number of 0s exceeds the number of 1s, so xy^2z is not in L, contradicting regularity. Thus, L is not regular.

Practice Exercise [EX_NET_05]
Target Skill: SKILL_ROUTING_CONGESTION
Difficulty Tier: MEDIUM
Problem Statement:
In TCP Reno congestion control, what triggers Fast Retransmit and Fast Recovery, and how is the Congestion Window (cwnd) adjusted compared to a timeout event?
Reference Solution & Rubric:
Fast Retransmit is triggered upon receiving 3 duplicate ACKs (4 identical ACKs total), signaling that a single packet was lost while subsequent packets arrived out-of-order. Instead of dropping cwnd to 1 MSS (as in a timeout), TCP Reno sets ssthresh = cwnd / 2, sets cwnd = ssthresh + 3 MSS (Fast Recovery), retransmits the missing segment, and increments cwnd by 1 MSS for each additional duplicate ACK received until an ACK acknowledging the new data arrives.
